items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like `buildWindowSpecSQL` and `validateFrameSpec` say what they do, but the new public helpers have no JSDoc, unlike the documented builder methods next to them. The nested ternary `isWindowSpec(spec) ? ... : (isSQLWrapper(spec) ? spec.getSQL() : sql`${spec}`)` is dense. One test is confusing: `dialect.sqlToQuery(...).sql ? undefined : undefined` with no assertions.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The identical `.window()` body, with its name validation and spec building, is copy-pasted into all 5 dialect select.ts files. The project brief asked for one shared helper (e.g. `assertValidWindowName`). The `sql`${spec}`` fallback can never run, and window.test.ts has a test with no assertions. The helpers are in sql/expressions, not the requested sql/functions.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: All required checks are there: ntile/nthValue reject non-positive integers, preceding/following reject bad numbers, frame order is checked through `offset` (with ±Infinity for the unbounded constants), and empty or whitespace-only window names are rejected. Numeric arguments are emitted via `sql.raw` after the integer check, so they never become bound parameters.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change only adds things. Each *SelectConfig gets an optional `window?: SQL[]`, and pg/mysql/sqlite/gel/singlestore all get the same `.window()` method. The WINDOW chunk is only emitted when windows exist, so queries without windows produce the same SQL as before. Everything is exported through sql/expressions/index.ts, and no existing signature changed.
